01Oral dosing

Taken by mouth, as a pill.

SELFTAC® degraders are designed to be small enough to be swallowed, not injected.

02In the gut

The dimer comes apart into two monomers.

In the gut, each SELFTAC® dimer dissociates at its reversible linker into two small monomers, which are absorbed.

03In the bloodstream

Monomers and dimer, in equilibrium.

In the plasma, two monomers keep joining into the dimer and coming apart again at the reversible linker: a dynamic equilibrium.

04The barrier

Only the monomers get through.

The dimer is too large to penetrate the cell membrane or the blood-brain barrier. Each small monomer passes through on its own.

05Ternary complex

Inside the cell, a dimer forms the ternary complex.

Monomers and dimers are in equilibrium here too. One dimer binds the target protein and an E3 ligase: a ternary complex.

06Degradation

Tagged, then broken down.

Ubiquitin marks the target and the proteasome destroys it. The degrader is free to find the next one.

Targeted protein degradation beyond conventional limits.
